Middle East.headline: Besieged Yemeni city Taiz faces acute food insecurity
Middle East.body: People in Yemen's Taiz have rushed to buy food as basic supplies are cut off due to the Houthi group's encirclement, driving up the prices of goods still left in the city. Despite the Houthis gaining control of the majority of Taiz Governorate, the provincial capital city of Taiz remains in the hands of the Yemeni government forces. The Houthis have imposed a tight military blockade on entry and exit points to the city. Deprived of supply routes, the residents of Taiz are struggling to obtain basic food supplies. Middle East.headline: Cholera outbreak spreading rapidly in Yemen as more people flee violence
Middle East.body: Cholera cases have tripled in the last three weeks in southern Yemen as the conflict and displacement escalates, and Islamic Relief is warning that thousands of lives are at risk. The fighting has caused over 200,000 people to seek refuge in overcrowded and polluted camps and other sites such as mosques and schools. About 40% of the displaced people do not have access to safe water and one third don’t have proper latrines, forcing families to defecate outside – conditions that are breeding grounds for the spread of fatal water-borne diseases such as cholera.

Africa.headline: DRC / Regional — Ebola Outbreak Spreads as Fatality Toll Surpasses 4,400
Africa.body: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is experiencing the deadliest and fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in its history, driven by the Bundibugyo strain for which no approved vaccine or specific treatment exists. European health figures indicate the outbreak has caused 9,144 confirmed cases and 4,410 deaths since May. Active transmission has expanded to eight Congolese provinces and crossed borders into four countries, with Kenya confirming its second case. Response efforts remain severely hampered by local violence, population displacement, and challenges in contact tracing. Epidemiologists warn that children are disproportionately affected, representing nearly one in four confirmed cases in North Kivu province.

Africa.headline: Sudan — Drone Strike Kills 32 Displaced Civilians in Blue Nile State
Africa.body: A drone strike killed 32 displaced civilians, including 26 women, near the Abu Shandi shelter in Sudan's Blue Nile State on October 9. The explosive shell struck a seasonal riverbed near Ad-Damazin where displaced men, women, and children were sifting for gold to sustain themselves. The attack underscores acute civilian protection risks facing displaced populations in eastern Sudan who are forced to engage in informal work near temporary displacement sites.

Asia-Pacific.headline: Afghanistan — UNICEF warns acute child malnutrition to reach 5-year high in 2027
Asia-Pacific.body: Acute malnutrition is worsening rapidly across Afghanistan, with over four million children projected to require treatment in 2027, according to the Afghanistan Nutrition Cluster co-chaired by UNICEF and Action Against Hunger. Latest IPC projections indicate that more than one million children will suffer from severe acute malnutrition, while nearly 1.3 million pregnant and breastfeeding mothers will also experience acute malnutrition. The number of provinces suffering critical malnutrition levels has increased from seven in 2025 to 10 in 2026, and is expected to reach 14 in 2027. The emergency is fueled by severe foreign aid reductions, soaring food prices, and persistent poverty.

Asia-Pacific.headline: Afghanistan — High displacement numbers persist despite surge in fragile returns
Asia-Pacific.body: Afghanistan remains one of the primary sources of forcibly displaced people globally, with Afghanistan, Syria, and Sudan together accounting for more than 70 percent of individuals requiring international protection, according to the UN Global Trends Report. Although a significant increase in returns to Afghanistan contributed to 14.7 million displaced people returning to their home areas globally in 2025, the report warned that many returnees faced severe pressure and returned under extremely fragile conditions without adequate protection or support.

Asia-Pacific.headline: Myanmar — Nearly 70 percent of junta airstrikes targeted civilian areas
Asia-Pacific.body: An analysis covering military operations between January 2024 and July 2026 revealed that nearly 70 percent of aerial strikes by Myanmar's military junta targeted civilian populations. According to a report by BNI-MPM, the military regime has increasingly launched air raids against communities following battlefield losses, lost military posts, or at the end of the rainy season. Analysts stated that the tactic aims to weaken civilian support for resistance groups by systematically punishing communities located near opposition positions.

Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: DRC / Regional — Bundibugyo Ebola Outbreak Spreads as Children Suffer Disproportionate Impact
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: An Ebola outbreak centered in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, caused by the Bundibugyo strain, has spread across borders, with Kenya confirming its second case in a 39-year-old relative. The variant carries a case-fatality rate approaching 50 percent, with no specific vaccine or treatment currently available. According to Doctors Without Borders, children in DRC's North Kivu province are disproportionately affected, with nearly one in four confirmed cases occurring in children under five. MSF highlighted that children face higher mortality rates than adults and remain largely excluded from vaccines, treatments, and clinical trial access.

Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Nepal — Flash Floods Destroy Central Villages Following River-Blocking Landslide
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: A pre-dawn landslide blocked the Budhi Gandaki River on 11 October, triggering severe downstream flash floods in Nepal's central Gorkha district. River levels rose from two to nearly 8.5 meters within hours, destroying two villages in Chumanubri rural municipality and washing away homes, roads, and bridges. According to national disaster risk management authorities, 204 homes were damaged and over 650 people were affected. In addition, more than 100 foreign trekkers were stranded in the hiking area, and part of a local hydropower station sustained damage.

Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Türkiye — Heavy Rains and Severe Flooding Cause Fatalities and Evacuations in Istanbul
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: Torrential rainfall and severe flash flooding battered Istanbul, Türkiye, over two days, leading to casualties and widespread evacuations. Emergency teams received 8,515 calls and evacuated 595 people trapped by floodwaters in homes and facilities across districts such as Göktürk, Kemerburgaz, and Ayazağa. The Associated Press reported three deaths resulting from the heavy weather, while local officials confirmed at least two flood-related fatalities, including a 34-year-old man in Sarıyer district and a 14-year-old boy.
